frontier.hypothesis: A second byte-free, flow-counted out2 read exists in the MID basic block (block 2), giving out2 4 refs / live 48-54 (pri 1666-1481, inside the window) while MID's stptr init still reads pa4 and emits target's addiu s3,s7,32.
frontier.mechanism: global.c allocno priority; crucially, MID is its own cse basic block, so cse1 has NO qty knowledge that out2 == pa4+0x20 there (banked s3 evidence) - an out2-reading expression in MID is NOT constant-folded the way the same expression is inside block 0.
frontier.next_probe: Read .cse/.cse2/.combine for the MID block FIRST (the s3 'everything folds pre-flow' conclusion was drawn on block-0 semantics and has never been re-measured for block 2, nor with the corrected arithmetic). Then enumerate out2-reading MID expressions whose emitted form is one of MID's six target insns.

frontier.mechanism: the copy survives because out2's staged value is live across loop2's back edge, so post-flow copy propagation cannot fold it into the single use at func_800523E0.
frontier.next_probe: Dump .combine/.jump2/.greg for rejected/staging-position-sweep-133insn.c and identify which pass declines the coalesce; then try spellings that keep the long live range but make def and use copy-propagable - e.g. a staging def on the loop2 back edge (the first iteration legitimately uses the preamble value, since out2 and loop2's stptr both hold pa4 + 0x20).

frontier.mechanism: same global.c priority ordering, but the whole allocno set is different (out2 absorbs the 10-ref merged pseudo) - a world s1-s4 never analysed.
frontier.next_probe: Re-derive the FULL disposition goal for the V1 chassis from scratch with the corrected formula (.lreg/.greg), then solve for the minimal ref/live perturbation set the way s2/s3 did for the split model.
